name: Alabama
origin: From the Alabama (Alibamu) people; often glossed from Choctaw as “thicket clearers.”

name: Alaska
origin: From Aleut/Unangan “Alaxsxaq” — roughly “the mainland.”

name: Arizona
origin: Likely from O’odham “ali ṣonak” (small spring); a Basque origin is also proposed.

name: Arkansas
origin: A French rendering of a Sioux word for the Quapaw people.

name: California
origin: From a mythical island in the 1510 Spanish romance “Las Sergas de Esplandián.”

sites.name: Golden Gate Bridge
sites.fact: When it opened it was the longest suspension-bridge span on Earth. Its “International Orange” color was chosen partly for visibility in San Francisco’s fog.

sites.name: Alcatraz Island
sites.fact: “The Rock” held Al Capone and George “Machine Gun” Kelly. No confirmed successful escape was ever proven; the 1962 escape remains officially unsolved.

sites.name: Yosemite National Park
sites.fact: Lincoln signed the Yosemite Grant during the Civil War — the first time the U.S. set aside land specifically for preservation, seeding the national-park idea.

name: Colorado
origin: Spanish for “colored/reddish,” after the silt-laden Colorado River.

name: Connecticut
origin: From Mohegan-Pequot “quinnitukqut” — “at the long tidal river.”

name: Delaware
origin: For Lord De La Warr (Thomas West), an early governor of Virginia.

name: Florida
origin: Spanish “Pascua Florida” (Feast of Flowers/Easter), named by Ponce de León in 1513.

sites.name: Castillo de San Marcos
sites.fact: In St. Augustine — the oldest masonry fort in the continental U.S. Its walls are coquina, a soft shell-stone that absorbed cannonballs instead of shattering.

sites.name: Kennedy Space Center
sites.fact: Launch site for every crewed U.S. Moon mission and the Space Shuttle. Launch Complex 39A sent Apollo 11 skyward on July 16, 1969.

sites.name: St. Augustine (Old Town)
sites.fact: The oldest continuously occupied European-established settlement in the continental U.S. — predating Jamestown by 42 years.

name: Georgia
origin: Named for King George II of Great Britain.

name: Hawaii
origin: Possibly from “Hawaiki,” the legendary Polynesian homeland.

name: Idaho
origin: A coined word once claimed to be Shoshone; its true origin is disputed.

name: Illinois
origin: French rendering of the name of the Illinois (Illini) confederation.

name: Indiana
origin: Latin-style coinage meaning “Land of the Indians.”

name: Iowa
origin: From the Ioway (Iowa) people.

name: Kansas
origin: From the Kansa (Kaw) people — “people of the south wind.”

name: Kentucky
origin: From an Iroquoian word, often glossed “meadow land” or “land of tomorrow.”

name: Louisiana
origin: Named for King Louis XIV of France.

name: Maine
origin: Likely the nautical “mainland,” or the French province of Maine.

name: Maryland
origin: For Queen Henrietta Maria, wife of King Charles I.

name: Massachusetts
origin: From the Massachusett people — “at/near the great hill.”

sites.name: Faneuil Hall
sites.fact: Boston’s “Cradle of Liberty” — the meeting hall where colonists debated resistance to British taxes in the years before the Revolution.

sites.name: Plymouth Rock
sites.fact: The traditional landing spot of the Mayflower Pilgrims. The rock now sits under a granite portico at the water’s edge.

sites.name: USS Constitution
sites.fact: “Old Ironsides” — the world’s oldest commissioned warship still afloat. British shot seemed to bounce off her oak hull in the War of 1812.

name: Michigan
origin: From Ojibwe “mishigami” — “large water” (the Great Lakes).

name: Minnesota
origin: From Dakota “mni sota” — “cloudy” or “sky-tinted” water.

name: Mississippi
origin: From Ojibwe “misi-ziibi” — “great river.”

name: Missouri
origin: From the Missouria people — “people of the big canoes.”

name: Montana
origin: From Spanish/Latin “montaña” — “mountain.”

name: Nebraska
origin: From Otoe/Omaha “ñí brásge” — “flat water” (the Platte River).

name: Nevada
origin: Spanish “nevada” — “snow-covered,” from the Sierra Nevada.

name: New Hampshire
origin: Named for the English county of Hampshire.

name: New Jersey
origin: Named for the Channel Island of Jersey.

name: New Mexico
origin: Spanish “Nuevo México,” used long before the modern country of Mexico existed.

name: New York
origin: For the Duke of York (later King James II), after the English took New Amsterdam.

sites.name: Statue of Liberty
sites.fact: A gift from France designed by Frédéric-Auguste Bartholdi. Its internal iron skeleton was engineered by Gustave Eiffel, who later built his tower in Paris.

sites.name: Ellis Island
sites.fact: The nation’s busiest immigration station until 1954 — roughly 12 million people passed through its Great Hall on their way into America.

sites.name: 9/11 Memorial & One WTC
sites.fact: Twin reflecting pools sit in the footprints of the original towers. One World Trade Center rises to 1,776 feet — a nod to 1776.

sites.name: Niagara Falls State Park
sites.fact: The oldest state park in the United States, laid out by Frederick Law Olmsted — the landscape architect behind Central Park.

name: North Carolina
origin: For King Charles I (Latin “Carolus”).

name: North Dakota
origin: From the Dakota (Sioux) people — “friend/ally.”

name: Ohio
origin: From Seneca “ohi:yo’” — “great river.”

name: Oklahoma
origin: From Choctaw “okla humma” — “red people.”

name: Oregon
origin: Origin genuinely uncertain; several competing theories exist.

name: Pennsylvania
origin: “Penn’s Woods” — honoring Admiral William Penn, father of founder William Penn.

sites.name: Independence Hall
sites.fact: In Philadelphia — both the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the U.S. Constitution (1787) were debated and adopted inside this red-brick building.

sites.name: Liberty Bell
sites.fact: Famous for its jagged crack. Its inscription — “proclaim liberty throughout all the land” — made it an icon for abolitionists in the 1800s.

sites.name: Gettysburg Battlefield
sites.fact: Site of the Civil War’s bloodiest battle and, months later, Lincoln’s 272-word Gettysburg Address.

name: Rhode Island
origin: Possibly for Aquidneck’s likeness to Rhodes, or Dutch “Roodt Eylandt” (red island).

name: South Carolina
origin: For King Charles I (Latin “Carolus”).

name: South Dakota
origin: From the Dakota (Sioux) people — “friend/ally.”

name: Tennessee
origin: From the Cherokee town name “Tanasi.”

name: Texas
origin: From Caddo “táysha” — “friends/allies.”

sites.name: The Alamo
sites.fact: A former Spanish mission in San Antonio. Its 1836 siege — and the cry “Remember the Alamo!” — became the rallying point of the Texas Revolution.

sites.name: San Jacinto Monument
sites.fact: Marks where Texas won its independence in an 18-minute battle. At 567 feet, the column is topped by a Lone Star and stands taller than the Washington Monument.

name: Utah
origin: From the Ute people.

name: Vermont
origin: From French “vert mont” — “green mountain.”

name: Virginia
origin: For Elizabeth I, England’s “Virgin Queen.”

name: Washington
origin: For George Washington — the only U.S. state named after a president.

name: West Virginia
origin: Split from Virginia during the Civil War; keeps the Virginia name.

name: Wisconsin
origin: A French rendering of a Miami/Ojibwe river name; exact meaning uncertain.

name: Wyoming
origin: From a Delaware (Lenape) word for “large prairie place,” via Pennsylvania’s Wyoming Valley.

name: Washington, D.C.
origin: “Columbia” honors Christopher Columbus; the District was established by the Residence Act of 1790.

sites.name: Lincoln Memorial
sites.fact: Its 19-foot marble Lincoln faces the Mall. On its steps in 1963, Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the “I Have a Dream” speech.

sites.name: Washington Monument
sites.fact: A 555-foot marble obelisk. A funding gap mid-build left a visible color change in the stone about a third of the way up.

sites.name: U.S. Capitol
sites.fact: Home of Congress. Its cast-iron dome was completed during the Civil War — Lincoln insisted work continue as a sign the Union would endure.

sites.name: The White House
sites.fact: Every president except George Washington has lived here. British troops burned it in 1814; it was rebuilt and reoccupied by 1817.
